title: Login Flow
description: The auth frontend module shall provide a complete login flow for all users.
rationale: Users must be able to authenticate before accessing any protected resource in the system.

title: Logout Flow
description: The auth frontend module shall provide a logout action that terminates the user session.
rationale: Users must be able to end their session to protect account security on shared devices.

title: Password Reset Request Flow
description: The auth frontend module shall provide a password reset request flow for unauthenticated users.
rationale: Users who forget their password need a self-service path to regain account access without admin intervention.

title: Password Reset Confirm Flow
description: The auth frontend module shall provide a password reset confirmation flow accepting a token and new password.
rationale: Users clicking a reset link must be able to set a new password and immediately regain access.

title: Consent Gate Flow
description: The auth frontend module shall enforce AI processing consent before students access protected routes.
rationale: Regulatory and ethical obligations require explicit student consent before AI-driven processing of their data.

title: Route Guards
description: The auth frontend module shall enforce role-based access control on all client-side routes.
rationale: Preventing unauthorized route access on the client reduces accidental data exposure and improves security posture.

title: API Client Authorization Header
description: The auth frontend module shall attach an authorization credential to every API request.
rationale: The backend requires a valid Bearer token on all protected endpoints; omitting it results in 401 errors.

title: CSRF Token Propagation
description: The auth frontend module shall include the anti-CSRF credential on all state-changing API requests.
rationale: The backend CSRF middleware rejects POST/PATCH/DELETE/PUT requests without a matching X-CSRF-Token header, preventing cross-site request forgery.

title: Global Loading Indicator
description: The auth frontend module shall display a loading indicator during every async API operation.
rationale: Without a loading indicator, users cannot distinguish a slow network response from a frozen UI, leading to duplicate submissions.

title: Login Form Fields
description: The auth frontend module shall render a login form with username field, password field, and submit button.
rationale: The backend login endpoint requires both username and password; the form must expose both inputs to the user.

title: Login Form Submission
description: The auth frontend module shall submit the user's credentials when the login form is submitted.
rationale: Submitting credentials to the correct endpoint is the entry point for the authentication flow.

title: Login Success Credential Storage
description: The auth frontend module shall store the session credentials received after a successful login.
rationale: Storing the token in memory rather than localStorage reduces XSS token-theft risk while keeping the session usable.

title: Login Role-Based Redirect
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect students to /dashboard and admins to /admin after successful login.
rationale: Each role has a distinct landing page; routing users to the wrong page wastes time and exposes unintended UI.

title: Login 401 Error Display
description: The auth frontend module shall display an inline error and preserve the username field on a 401 login response.
rationale: Users who mistype a password should not have to retype their username; the inline error targets the credential mistake precisely.

title: Login Network Error Display
description: The auth frontend module shall display a server-unreachable error message when the login request fails due to a network error.
rationale: A blank or frozen form gives users no actionable information; a clear error message prompts them to retry.

title: Login Submit Button Disabled During Request
description: The auth frontend module shall disable the submit button while a login request is pending.
rationale: Disabling the button prevents duplicate submissions that would generate redundant sessions.

title: Login Empty Field Validation
description: The auth frontend module shall prevent login form submission when either the username or password field is empty.
rationale: Submitting empty credentials would produce a 400 from the server; client-side validation avoids a needless round-trip.

title: Login 500 Error Display
description: The auth frontend module shall display a generic error message on a 500 login response.
rationale: Server errors should surface to the user so they know the failure is not due to their input and can retry later.

title: Logout Button Placement
description: The auth frontend module shall render a logout button in the navigation bar for authenticated users.
rationale: The logout action must be consistently reachable from any page so users can end sessions without navigating away.

title: Logout API Call
description: The auth frontend module shall send a logout request to the server when the user logs out.
rationale: The server must invalidate the session token; a client-side-only logout leaves the token valid and reusable.

title: Logout State Clear
description: The auth frontend module shall clear the stored authorization credentials and anti-CSRF state after a successful logout response.
rationale: Residual auth state after logout would allow subsequent requests to succeed under the former session.

title: Logout Redirect
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect to /login after clearing auth state on successful logout.
rationale: After logout the user is unauthenticated; remaining on a protected page would trigger a redirect anyway, so redirecting immediately gives a clean experience.

title: Password Reset Request Form
description: The auth frontend module shall render a password reset request form with a username field and submit button.
rationale: Users who cannot log in need a dedicated form to initiate a reset; it must require only their username.

title: Password Reset Request API Call
description: The auth frontend module shall submit the username to initiate a password reset on form submission.
rationale: The backend requires a POST to the request endpoint with the username to initiate the reset flow.

title: Password Reset Request Success Message
description: The auth frontend module shall display a neutral confirmation message on any 2xx reset request response.
rationale: Revealing whether an account exists would allow username enumeration; the same message must appear regardless of account existence.

title: Password Reset Request Rate Limit Display
description: The auth frontend module shall display a rate-limit error message on a 429 reset request response.
rationale: Users need to know they must wait before retrying, preventing them from submitting the form repeatedly.

title: Password Reset Request Empty Field Validation
description: The auth frontend module shall prevent reset request submission when the username field is empty.
rationale: Submitting an empty username produces a 400 from the server; client-side validation avoids a needless round-trip.

title: Password Reset Confirm Form Fields
description: The auth frontend module shall render a reset confirm form with a token field and a new password field.
rationale: The confirm endpoint requires both a token and a new password; the form must expose both inputs.

title: Password Reset Confirm Token Pre-fill
description: The auth frontend module shall pre-fill the token field from the token query parameter on page load.
rationale: Users clicking a reset link expect the token to be applied automatically; requiring manual entry creates friction and errors.

title: Password Reset Confirm API Call
description: The auth frontend module shall submit the reset token and new password on confirm form submission.
rationale: The backend confirm endpoint requires both fields; sending the correct payload is necessary for the reset to succeed.

title: Password Reset Confirm Success Redirect
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect to /login with a success banner on a 204 confirm response.
rationale: After a successful reset the user must log in with their new password; a success banner confirms the change was applied.

title: Password Reset Confirm 400 Error Display
description: The auth frontend module shall display an invalid-or-expired error on a 400 confirm response.
rationale: A 400 from the confirm endpoint means the token is invalid or expired; the user needs a specific message to initiate a new reset.

title: Password Reset Confirm Empty Field Validation
description: The auth frontend module shall prevent confirm form submission when the token or new password field is empty.
rationale: Submitting empty fields produces a 400 from the server; client-side validation avoids a needless round-trip.

title: Consent Screen Content
description: The auth frontend module shall display AI processing consent text and an accept button on the consent screen.
rationale: Students must be presented with the consent text before accepting; an accept button without text would not constitute informed consent.

title: Consent API Call
description: The auth frontend module shall send a consent acceptance request when the accept button is activated.
rationale: The consent endpoint is authenticated and CSRF-protected; omitting either header results in a 401 or 403 rejection.

title: Consent Success Redirect
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect to /dashboard after a 204 consent response.
rationale: Once consent is recorded the student is cleared to use the platform and should land on their dashboard.

title: Consent Guard Redirect
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect students without recorded consent to /consent on protected routes.
rationale: Allowing unconsented students to access other routes would bypass the legal and ethical consent requirement.

title: Consent Version Payload
description: The auth frontend module shall include a non-empty version identifier in the consent acceptance request.
rationale: The backend requires a version field; omitting it produces a 400 and the consent is not recorded.

title: Consent 500 Error Display
description: The auth frontend module shall display a generic error when the consent acceptance request fails.
rationale: A server error during consent recording means the student has not been cleared; they must not be silently redirected to the dashboard.

title: Unauthenticated Protected Route Guard
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect unauthenticated users to /login when accessing any protected route.
rationale: Unauthenticated users have no valid session; allowing them to reach protected pages exposes content they are not authorized to see.

title: Student Admin Route Guard
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect students accessing admin routes to /dashboard.
rationale: Admin routes expose user management controls that students must not access.

title: Admin Student Route Guard
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect admins accessing student routes to /admin.
rationale: Student routes are scoped to individual learner data; admins should use the admin interface instead.

title: Global 401 Auth State Clear
description: The auth frontend module shall clear stored auth credentials on any expired-session API response.
rationale: A 401 on a protected route means the session has expired or been revoked; retaining stale auth state would cause further failures.

title: API Client Bearer Header on All Requests
description: The auth frontend module shall attach an authorization credential to every outgoing API request.
rationale: The backend rejects protected requests without a valid Authorization header; every request must carry the token.

title: In-Memory Token Storage
description: The auth frontend module shall store the session token exclusively in memory, not in browser storage.
rationale: Storing tokens in Web Storage exposes them to XSS attacks; memory storage limits the token's accessibility to the current page context.

title: Token Clear on Logout
description: The auth frontend module shall remove the in-memory session token when the user logs out.
rationale: Residual in-memory token after logout would allow subsequent API calls to succeed under a terminated session.

title: CSRF Cookie Name
description: The auth frontend module shall read the CSRF value from the designated cookie after login.
rationale: The backend sets the CSRF token in the __Host-csrf cookie; reading the wrong cookie name yields an empty or incorrect value.

title: CSRF Header on State-Changing Requests
description: The auth frontend module shall include the anti-CSRF credential on every state-changing request.
rationale: The backend CSRF middleware rejects any state-changing request that lacks a matching X-CSRF-Token header with a 403.

title: CSRF Header Value Matches Cookie
description: The auth frontend module shall set the anti-CSRF credential to match the stored anti-CSRF value exactly.
rationale: The backend performs a byte-for-byte comparison of the cookie value and the header; any discrepancy returns a 403.

title: CSRF State Clear on Logout
description: The auth frontend module shall clear the stored anti-CSRF credential when the user logs out.
rationale: Retaining the CSRF token after logout could allow it to be submitted on subsequent unauthenticated requests.

title: Loading Indicator Shown During Request
description: The auth frontend module shall display a visible loading indicator when any async API call is pending.
rationale: Users need visual feedback that the system is processing their action so they do not interpret a delay as inactivity.

title: Loading Indicator Hidden After Response
description: The auth frontend module shall hide the loading indicator once an API call resolves or rejects.
rationale: A persistent loading indicator after a completed request misleads the user into thinking the operation is still running.

title: Login Success CSRF Capture
description: The auth frontend module shall capture the anti-CSRF value received after a successful login.
rationale: The server sets the CSRF token on login; the client must capture it before issuing any subsequent state-changing request.

title: Login Loading Indicator During Request
description: The auth frontend module shall display a loading indicator while a login request is pending.
rationale: Visual feedback reassures the user the submission was accepted and the system is responding.

title: Global 401 Redirect to Login
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect to the login page after clearing expired-session credentials.
rationale: After clearing an expired session the user must re-authenticate; the login page is the correct destination.

title: Login Username Field Present
description: The auth frontend module shall render a text input for username on the login page.
rationale: The login endpoint requires a username; the form must expose this input for the user to enter their credentials.

title: Login Password Field Present
description: The auth frontend module shall render a password-type input for password on the login page.
rationale: Displaying the password as plain text would allow shoulder-surfing; a password-type input masks the value.

title: Login Submit Button Present
description: The auth frontend module shall render a submit button on the login form.
rationale: Users need a clearly labelled action trigger to submit the login form.

title: Login Request Method and URL
description: The auth frontend module shall send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login on form submission.
rationale: The backend login handler is registered on POST /api/v1/auth/login; any other method or path returns 404 or 405.

title: Login Request Body Shape
description: The auth frontend module shall send JSON body {"username": string, "password": string} in the login POST.
rationale: The backend decodes exactly those two fields; extra or missing fields cause a 400 bad request response.

title: Login Request Content-Type Header
description: The auth frontend module shall set Content-Type: application/json on the login POST request.
rationale: The backend uses json.NewDecoder which requires the body to be valid JSON; an incorrect Content-Type can cause parsing failures.

title: Login Token Extraction from 200 Response
description: The auth frontend module shall extract the token field from the 200 login response body and store it in memory.
rationale: The response body contains the Bearer token under the key "token"; it must be stored for use on subsequent requests.

title: Login Role Extraction from 200 Response
description: The auth frontend module shall extract the role field from the 200 login response body and store it in memory.
rationale: The role value determines which route the user is redirected to and which UI elements are shown.

title: CSRF Cookie Read After Login
description: The auth frontend module shall read the __Host-csrf cookie value and store it in memory after a 200 login response.
rationale: The server sets the CSRF cookie on login; the client must capture it before issuing any subsequent state-changing request.

title: Student Login Redirect
description: The auth frontend module shall navigate to /dashboard when the login response role equals "student".
rationale: Students land on their course dashboard after login; redirecting elsewhere would confuse the expected post-login flow.

title: Admin Login Redirect
description: The auth frontend module shall navigate to /admin when the login response role equals "admin".
rationale: Admins land on the admin panel after login; redirecting to /dashboard would present a student-scoped UI to an admin.

title: Login 401 Inline Error Text
description: The auth frontend module shall display "Invalid username or password." inline in the login form on a 401 response.
rationale: The exact error string must match the design specification so QA automation can assert the element text precisely.

title: Login 401 Username Field Preserved
description: The auth frontend module shall retain the username field value after a 401 login response.
rationale: Clearing the username on a password error forces the user to retype information they entered correctly, creating unnecessary friction.

title: Login Network Error Text
description: The auth frontend module shall display "Unable to reach server. Please try again." on a network error.
rationale: The exact string must be specified so tests can assert it; a vague message does not help users understand the failure.

title: Login Submit Button Disabled During Request
description: The auth frontend module shall disable the login submit button while a login request is in flight.
rationale: Allowing re-submission while a request is pending could create duplicate sessions or confuse the user with multiple error states.

title: Login Loading Indicator During Request
description: The auth frontend module shall show a loading indicator adjacent to the login form while the login request is pending.
rationale: Visual feedback reassures the user the submission was accepted and the system is responding.

title: Login Client-Side Empty Field Block
description: The auth frontend module shall not submit the login form when either the username or password field is empty.
rationale: An empty-field submission always fails with a 400; preventing it client-side avoids a wasted network round-trip.

title: Login 500 Error Text
description: The auth frontend module shall display "Something went wrong. Please try again later." on a 500 login response.
rationale: A server-error message distinct from the credential-error message prevents user confusion about whether their password is wrong.

title: Logout Button in Nav
description: The auth frontend module shall render a logout button in the navigation bar when the user is authenticated.
rationale: The logout action must be visible from every authenticated page; placing it in the nav bar provides consistent access.

title: Logout Request Method and URL
description: The auth frontend module shall send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/logout when the logout button is activated.
rationale: The backend logout handler is registered on POST /api/v1/auth/logout; a GET or DELETE would return 405.

title: Logout Request Authorization Header
description: The auth frontend module shall include the Authorization: Bearer <token> header in the logout POST request.
rationale: The backend extracts the token from the Authorization header to identify and invalidate the session; a missing header returns 401.

title: Logout Clears Bearer Token
description: The auth frontend module shall set the in-memory Bearer token to null after a 204 logout response.
rationale: Retaining the token after logout allows the now-invalid token to be sent on subsequent requests, which would return 401 errors.

title: Logout Clears CSRF Token
description: The auth frontend module shall set the in-memory CSRF token value to null after a 204 logout response.
rationale: The CSRF token is tied to the authenticated session; retaining it after logout could permit unintended state-changing requests.

title: Logout Navigation to Login
description: The auth frontend module shall navigate to /login after clearing auth state following a successful logout.
rationale: After logout the user is unauthenticated; /login is the only appropriate destination.

title: Reset Request Username Field
description: The auth frontend module shall render a text input for username on the password reset request page.
rationale: The reset request endpoint requires the username field; the form must expose this input.

title: Reset Request Submit Button
description: The auth frontend module shall render a submit button on the password reset request form.
rationale: Users need an explicit action trigger to submit the reset request.

title: Reset Request Method and URL
description: The auth frontend module shall send a POST to /api/v1/password-reset/request on reset request form submission.
rationale: The backend password reset handler is registered on POST /api/v1/password-reset/request; any other path or method fails.

title: Reset Request Body Shape
description: The auth frontend module shall send JSON body {"username": string} in the password reset request POST.
rationale: The backend decodes only the username field; omitting it or sending extra fields causes a 400 response.

title: Reset Request 204 Success Message
description: The auth frontend module shall display "If that account exists, a reset link has been sent." on a 204 response.
rationale: The exact neutral string must be specified to allow QA automation to assert the message without confirming account existence.

title: Reset Request Success Message for All 2xx
description: The auth frontend module shall display the neutral confirmation message for any 2xx reset request response.
rationale: Future server changes may return 200 with a body; the client must treat any 2xx as success to stay compatible.

title: Reset Request 429 Rate Limit Message
description: The auth frontend module shall display "Too many requests. Please wait before trying again." on a 429 response.
rationale: Users must be told explicitly to wait; a generic error would not communicate the need to delay before retrying.

title: Reset Request Client-Side Empty Field Block
description: The auth frontend module shall not submit the reset request form when the username field is empty.
rationale: An empty username always produces a 400; blocking submission client-side avoids a wasted round-trip.

title: Reset Confirm Token Field
description: The auth frontend module shall render a text input for the reset token on the password reset confirm page.
rationale: The confirm endpoint requires the token field; the form must expose it so users can verify or edit it.

title: Reset Confirm New Password Field
description: The auth frontend module shall render a password-type input for the new password on the reset confirm page.
rationale: The confirm endpoint requires new_password; the input must mask the value to prevent shoulder-surfing.

title: Reset Confirm Submit Button
description: The auth frontend module shall render a submit button on the password reset confirm form.
rationale: Users need an explicit action trigger to submit the new password.

title: Reset Confirm Token Pre-fill from Query Param
description: The auth frontend module shall populate the token field with the token URL query parameter on page load.
rationale: Reset links include ?token=<value>; pre-filling avoids copy-paste errors and reduces friction for the user.

title: Reset Confirm Request Method and URL
description: The auth frontend module shall send a POST to /api/v1/password-reset/confirm on confirm form submission.
rationale: The backend confirm handler is registered on POST /api/v1/password-reset/confirm; any other method or path fails.

title: Reset Confirm Request Body Shape
description: The auth frontend module shall send JSON body {"token": string, "new_password": string} in the confirm POST.
rationale: The backend decodes exactly token and new_password; omitting or misnaming either field causes a 400 response.

title: Reset Confirm 204 Redirect to Login
description: The auth frontend module shall navigate to /login after a 204 confirm password reset response.
rationale: After a successful reset the user must log in with their new credentials; /login is the correct destination.

title: Reset Confirm Success Banner on Login Page
description: The auth frontend module shall display "Password updated. Please log in." banner on the /login page after a successful reset.
rationale: The exact banner text confirms the reset completed and prompts the user to authenticate with their new password.

title: Reset Confirm 400 Error Text
description: The auth frontend module shall display "Reset link is invalid or expired." on a 400 confirm response.
rationale: A 400 means the token was not found or has expired; the message must direct the user to request a new link.

title: Reset Confirm Client-Side Empty Field Block
description: The auth frontend module shall not submit the confirm form when the token or new password field is empty.
rationale: Submitting empty fields causes a 400; blocking client-side prevents unnecessary round-trips.

title: Consent Screen AI Text
description: The auth frontend module shall display AI processing consent text before the accept button on the consent screen.
rationale: Informed consent requires the user to read the terms before acting; the text must precede the accept action.

title: Consent Screen Accept Button
description: The auth frontend module shall render an accept button on the consent screen.
rationale: The accept button is the user's explicit signal of consent; the system must provide a clear, single action to record it.

title: Consent Request Method and URL
description: The auth frontend module shall send a POST to /api/v1/consent when the accept button is activated.
rationale: The backend consent handler is registered on POST /api/v1/consent; any other method or path returns 404 or 405.

title: Consent Request Authorization Header
description: The auth frontend module shall include Authorization: Bearer <token> in the consent POST request.
rationale: The consent endpoint is authenticated; omitting the Authorization header returns a 401 and the consent is not recorded.

title: Consent Request CSRF Header
description: The auth frontend module shall include X-CSRF-Token in the consent POST request.
rationale: The consent endpoint is protected by the CSRF middleware; omitting the header causes a 403 and the consent is not recorded.

title: Consent 204 Redirect to Dashboard
description: The auth frontend module shall navigate to /dashboard after a 204 consent response.
rationale: A 204 confirms the consent was recorded; the student is cleared to use the platform and should land on their dashboard.

title: Consent Guard on Protected Routes
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect a student with no recorded consent to /consent on any non-consent protected route.
rationale: The consent gate must be enforced before the student can reach any platform content requiring AI processing consent.

title: Consent Version in Request Body
description: The auth frontend module shall send JSON body {"version": string} with a non-empty version in the consent POST.
rationale: The backend rejects a consent POST with an empty or absent version field with a 400, leaving the student blocked at the consent gate.

title: Consent 500 Error Text
description: The auth frontend module shall display "Something went wrong. Please try again." on a 500 consent response.
rationale: A server error means consent was not recorded; the student must not be silently redirected as if consent had succeeded.

title: Unauthenticated Route Guard Check
description: The auth frontend module shall evaluate whether a Bearer token is present before rendering any protected route.
rationale: Without checking for a token the router cannot distinguish authenticated from unauthenticated users.

title: Unauthenticated Guard Redirect Target
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect to /login when no Bearer token is present and a protected route is requested.
rationale: /login is the only publicly accessible authentication entry point; all unauthenticated users must be directed there.

title: Student Blocked from Admin Routes
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect to /dashboard when a user with role student requests an admin route.
rationale: Admin routes expose controls that students are not authorized to see; redirecting to /dashboard keeps them in their permitted area.

title: Admin Blocked from Student Routes
description: The auth frontend module shall redirect to /admin when a user with role admin requests a student route.
rationale: Student routes are scoped to learner data; admins operating there would interact with the wrong interface.

title: Global 401 Auth State Clear
description: The auth frontend module shall clear the in-memory Bearer token and CSRF token on any 401 API response.
rationale: A 401 means the session is no longer valid; retaining stale credentials would cause every subsequent request to fail with 401.

title: Global 401 Redirect to Login
description: The auth frontend module shall navigate to /login after clearing auth state on a 401 API response.
rationale: After clearing an expired session the user must re-authenticate; /login is the correct destination.

title: Authorization Header on Every Request
description: The auth frontend module shall set Authorization: Bearer <token> on every HTTP request made by the API client.
rationale: The backend requires a valid Authorization header on all protected endpoints; failing to include it on any request returns 401.

title: Token Not in Web Storage
description: The auth frontend module shall not write the Bearer token to localStorage or sessionStorage at any point.
rationale: Tokens in Web Storage are accessible to any same-origin script, making them vulnerable to XSS exfiltration.

title: Token Cleared on Logout
description: The auth frontend module shall nullify the in-memory token variable upon a successful logout response.
rationale: A non-null token after logout would be sent on any subsequent request, returning 401 until the page is refreshed.

title: CSRF Cookie Read by Exact Name
description: The auth frontend module shall read the CSRF token from the cookie named __Host-csrf after a successful login.
rationale: The backend sets the cookie with the exact name __Host-csrf; reading any other name yields an undefined or wrong value.

title: X-CSRF-Token Header on POST
description: The auth frontend module shall include the X-CSRF-Token header on every POST request.
rationale: The backend CSRF middleware validates this header on all non-safe HTTP methods; omitting it on POST returns 403.

title: X-CSRF-Token Header on PATCH DELETE PUT
description: The auth frontend module shall include the X-CSRF-Token header on every PATCH, DELETE, and PUT request.
rationale: The CSRF middleware applies to all state-changing methods; PATCH, DELETE, and PUT must carry the header or receive a 403.

title: CSRF Header Value Equals Cookie Value
description: The auth frontend module shall set X-CSRF-Token to the exact string value read from the __Host-csrf cookie.
rationale: The backend performs a constant-time byte comparison of the header and cookie; any deviation results in a 403.

title: CSRF Token Nullified on Logout
description: The auth frontend module shall set the in-memory CSRF token variable to null on a successful logout.
rationale: The CSRF token is bound to the authenticated session; clearing it prevents stale values from being sent after logout.

title: Loading Indicator Visible During Pending Request
description: The auth frontend module shall make a loading indicator visible before an API response is received.
rationale: Users must see feedback immediately after triggering an action; a delay before showing the indicator is indistinguishable from no feedback.

title: Loading Indicator Hidden After Resolution
description: The auth frontend module shall hide the loading indicator immediately after an API call resolves or rejects.
rationale: A loading indicator that persists after the operation ends misleads the user and blocks interaction with the form.
